headline: Thyrocare Technologies sells entire stake in wholly owned subsidiary Nueclear Healthcare
summary: Thyrocare Technologies has executed a share purchase agreement to sell its entire shareholding in its wholly owned subsidiary, Nueclear Healthcare Limited. Nueclear Healthcare is a diagnostic and healthcare services provider previously acquired by Thyrocare. The transaction alters Thyrocare's corporate structure as it exits this specific subsidiary business. Indian retail investors tracking Thyrocare should monitor the financial impact of this divestment on the parent company's upcoming earnings.
whats_next: Financial disclosures on sale proceeds and deal completion
why_it_matters: Subsidiary sale alters Thyrocare's asset base and future earnings profile.

headline: Thyrocare Q2 profit drops 68% due to one-time expenses
hook: Exceptional costs drag Thyrocare profits down
summary: Thyrocare Technologies reported a 68.2% year-on-year decline in net profit to ₹15.2 Cr for the September quarter. The sharp fall was primarily driven by a ₹45 Cr exceptional expense incurred during the period. Revenue performance and operational details were impacted by this significant one-time charge. The company is currently backed by PharmEasy.
why_it_matters: One-time costs hit bottom-line earnings for shareholders

summary: Several Indian companies released their Q2 earnings for the period ending September 2026. Milky Mist, Coal India, IEX, and Laurus Labs posted profit growth during the quarter. whats_next: Upcoming analyst earnings calls and management commentary
